transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-10-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes (recording started)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Alan Rivera (SentinelOps SRE), Priya Nair (Cloud Architect), Thomas Gray (Security)

Summary: short intake to understand SentinelOps requirements for private connectivity to Redwood (private endpoints vs peering), segmentation/isolation needs, and region constraints incl data residency. Focus on network topology, egress controls, and what baseline configs we need to provision a Private deployment.

Topics: private endpoints (privatelink/privatelink-like), VPC peering/transit, regional availability, egress control & proxies, audit/logging requirements, pentest readiness, timeline for pilot

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros? I'm Maya, AE on Redwood.
[00:12] Alan Rivera: Alan here, SRE at SentinelOps. We run the platform infra and will own the network hookup.
[00:16] Priya Nair: Priya, cloud architect, I'll handle VPC design and region gating.
[00:21] Thomas Gray: Thomas, security, focused on encryption, KMS, and third-party pentest constraints.
[00:25] Ravi Patel: Hi all, Ravi from Redwood SE, I'll dig into the network details and what we'll need for private endpoints.
[00:34] Maya Chen: Cool. The goal today is to figure out if we go with Redwood Private deployed into your VPC, or if a privatelink style endpoint + transit is better. Also to capture any region restrictions.
[00:45] Alan Rivera: Right. We can't do public internet egress for inference traffic — must be inside our accounts. We have a Transit GW in us-east-2, and on prem traffic routes via Direct Connect.
[00:58] Priya Nair: Also, data residency: certain datasets must stay within the EU for regulatory reasons. So if we run workloads that touch those datasets, those must be routed to eu-west-1 region.
[01:12] Ravi Patel: Understood. Two high-level options: 1) Redwood Private inside your VPCs (we provide an AMI or container bundle you run) or 2) Hosted but access via private endpoints/privatelink and VPC peering/transit to a Redwood-managed VPC. Each has different network handoffs.
[01:30] Thomas Gray: We prefer Redwood-managed control plane but with a private dataplane. Is that doable?
[01:36] Maya Chen: Yes, we have a hybrid option: control plane in Redwood, data plane in customer VPCs using private endpoints and dedicated instances. But that usually requires cross-account privatelink or peering depending on cloud provider.
[01:50] Alan Rivera: For AWS, we're strict about cross-account peering. We prefer interface endpoints for service exposure, not classic peering.
[01:57] Ravi Patel: Good note. Interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) are most common — we can accept inbound connections from, or we can host an endpoint service in our account that you connect to. Sometimes teams prefer the reverse: we host the service in your account as a managed SKU.
[02:12] Priya Nair: If you host your endpoint service in your account, that means we need to provision the subnets and SGs and ensure route tables don't leak, right?
[02:20] Ravi Patel: Yes, you'd provision subnets and SGs. We ask for 2 private subnets (AZ-redundant), specific security group rules (only from internal CIDR), and we give you an example CFN/Terraform snippet.
[02:32] Alan Rivera: What's the bandwidth profile like? Our inference traffic is bursty; some batches can saturate 2-3 Gbps on peak.
[02:41] Ravi Patel: Redwood Dedicated and Private support high throughput. For privatelink, traffic is NAT-ed through the interface endpoint ENIs; throughput depends on instance type and endpoint quotas. We usually recommend placing our inference fleet in the same region to avoid cross-region costs.
[02:58] Thomas Gray: Cross-region is a hard no for regulated data. So any datasets marked EU-only must never cross eu-west-1.
[03:06] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll need to map model hosting to region-specific clusters. We have EU clusters for eu-west-1. For hybrid flows, we can pin a model version to EU-only nodes.
[03:18] Priya Nair: How do you handle audit logs and flow logs? We need VPC flow logs ingested into our SIEM and request-level audit logs retained for 13 months.
[03:28] Ravi Patel: We can provide request-level logs from the dataplane (redacted PII) and we support exporting to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver or S3 via cross-account role. For VPC flow logs, you'll provide them; our SEs can use them for debugging.
[03:42] Alan Rivera: Pentest: we have a pentest program that will run an external and internal test. We need Redwood to provide an authorized scope, and we need to know if shared infra will be in scope.
[03:52] Maya Chen: We have a pentest consent process. For Private deployments in your VPC, it's your environment, so your pentest is fine. For Redwood-managed nodes, we provide the MP/owner contact and require coordination; for hosted we have a standard pentest addendum.
[04:06] Thomas Gray: KMS? Our policy mandates customer-managed CMKs for decrypting model inputs/outputs at rest.
[04:14] Ravi Patel: We can support customer-managed keys for data at rest when the dataplane is in your account. For hosted-only models we'd have Redwood-managed encryption; for Private deployments on customer infrastructure we integrate your KMS.
[04:28] Priya Nair: IP planning — we need to know what CIDR ranges your service will require so we can avoid overlap with our on-prem ranges.
[04:36] Ravi Patel: We'll provide a recommended non-overlapping CIDR for the service ENIs; typically a /28 per AZ for ENIs and endpoint allocations. We'll provide a spreadsheet template.
[04:48] Alan Rivera: Any special NAT or egress restrictions? We usually force egress through our proxy cluster.
[04:54] Maya Chen: If you have outbound egress to external model repos or updates, we can use an egress proxy or allow-list specific Redwood update hosts. For runtime inference traffic that must stay internal, we'll ensure the dataplane doesn't call external services.
[05:08] Priya Nair: A practical constraint: our Transit GW only allows attachments from approved accounts. How do we handle the account relationship?
[05:16] Ravi Patel: We often create a service account that is added to your approved account list; alternatively, we can provide a cross-account role for a customer-managed dataplane. Depends on your compliance stance.
[05:27] Thomas Gray: SLA expectations — given all this, what's the RTO and RPO? We have customers who require 99.95 for inference endpoints.
[05:36] Maya Chen: For Dedicated and Private with reserved capacity we support SLA targets; for the hybrid privatelink pattern SLA focuses on dataplane uptime in-provisioned AZs. We'll surface exact numbers in the enterprise contract.
[05:48] Alan Rivera: Are there any known gotchas with AWS STS/assume-role across accounts?
[05:54] Ravi Patel: Common gotcha is that STS sessions have a max duration that can affect long-lived connections for KV caches. We tend to set up short-lived roles for provisioning and instance profiles for long running nodes.
[06:10] Priya Nair: How much work on our side for certificate rotation and mTLS?
[06:15] Ravi Patel: We support mTLS between customer services and dataplane; for mTLS we can either manage certs with a trust anchor, or integrate with your cert management (hashicorp vault, AWS ACM). We'll document options.
[06:30] Thomas Gray: Does Redwood support VPC endpoint policies to restrict what APIs can be called over the interface endpoints?
[06:37] Ravi Patel: Yes, you can apply endpoint policies on interface endpoints. We also recommend security groups that restrict egress to only Redwood ENIs.
[06:46] Maya Chen: Quick check — timeline for pilot?
[06:50] Alan Rivera: We want a pilot in 6 weeks; internal approvals okay but security needs the pentest signoff and kinks ironed out.
[06:59] Maya Chen: Good. We'll treat this as a 6-week target. We'll scope a narrow pilot for eu-west-1 first for EU data and maybe us-east for non-regulated traffic.
[07:10] Priya Nair: Can we ask about model weights storage? We prefer weights encrypted with our KMS and never exported.
[07:18] Ravi Patel: If the dataplane runs in your account, weights sit on your storage and we can encrypt with your CMK. For hosted we offer model pinning and do not export weights to other regions if you request region isolation. Sometimes wording in our docs is a bit off — I mean, we can enforce region pinning.
[07:36] Alan Rivera: During the pilot we'll run some load tests; can Redwood provide a test harness or synthetic traffic generator?
[07:44] Ravi Patel: Yes, we have a perf harness and a script (JMeter-like) that we can run from your VPC. It emits typical tokenization patterns so we can tune batching.
[07:56] Thomas Gray: About cost — if we run customer-managed dataplane, what costs do we expect? Instance costs + Redwood platform fee?
[08:03] Maya Chen: Correct. Private deployment in your VPC means you bear infra costs; Redwood charges a platform fee and per-hour agent licensing. We'll share a cost-estimate spreadsheet.
[08:14] Priya Nair: One more compliance note: we need to ensure all access to logs is via our internal IAM principals only. Is that enforceable?
[08:22] Ravi Patel: Yes, when we export logs to your account we use cross-account roles and you control who can read them. For any logs stored in Redwood, we can provide RBAC and SSO-backed access controls.
[08:34] Maya Chen: Let's capture any blockers. Alan?
[08:37] Alan Rivera: Main blockers: Transit GW attachment approvals, pentest scoping ops, verify our CIDR won't overlap with any Redwood ENIs. Also a small policy question on CMK usage.
[08:47] Priya Nair: Also region gating for EU-only datasets.
[08:50] Maya Chen: Great. We'll send a checklist and a template for the VPC/VPN info. Ravi, can you note the technical items?
[08:58] Ravi Patel: Sure — I'll list out subnets (2 AZs), SG rules, required IAM roles, endpoint config example, and privatelink service name if we go that route.
[09:09] Thomas Gray: We might ask for a short written runbook for incident response for the pilot.
[09:14] Maya Chen: We'll add that to next steps.
[09:17] Alan Rivera: One small transcription correction in notes — I heard you say KV cache earlier, how does that flow with privatelink?
[09:24] Ravi Patel: KV cache is local to the inference instance; we persist checkpoints to customer storage in the Private deployment. With privatelink it's the same but the cache traffic stays internal to the VPC. Occasionally naming gets fuzzy in notes.
[09:38] Maya Chen: Anything else?
[09:40] Priya Nair: No, I think that's it. Thanks.
[09:43] Maya Chen: Recap: Ravi shares checklist and template, Maya attaches security docs and pricing, Alan shares flow logs and CIDR details, SentinelOps schedules internal pentest window. Target pilot in ~6 weeks.
[09:58] Alan Rivera: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:00] End of recording

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcribed product names (example: privatelink sometimes shows as 'private link'), filler words, and speaker overlaps. References: shared doc links - "Redwood Private networking checklist" (link placeholder), "privatelink example terraform" (link placeholder), cost estimate spreadsheet (link placeholder).
